question: Under Rule 520-4-.01(1), which body conducts all hearings in 'contested cases' as defined by the Georgia Administrative Procedure Act?
choice_a: The Office of State Administrative Hearings
choice_b: The Georgia Real Estate Commission's own internal hearing panel
choice_c: Fulton County Superior Court, as the court of first instance
choice_d: A jury trial in the county where the licensee resides
explanation: All hearings in 'contested cases' as defined by O.C.G.A. 50-13-13 shall be conducted by the Office of State Administrative Hearings, with the Commission initiating proceedings by filing pleadings there.

question: Per Rule 520-4-.02(3), what are the Commission office's normal business hours?
choice_a: 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., seven days a week
choice_b: 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, excluding weekends and legal holidays
choice_c: 7:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. on weekdays only
choice_d: 24 hours via the online portal only
explanation: The Commission office is open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. each weekday, except Saturdays, Sundays, legal holidays, and other state-office closures.

question: Under Rule 520-4-.02(6), when a computed time period is seven days or less, how are intervening Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays treated?
choice_b: They are always included, regardless of the period's length
choice_c: They are excluded from the computation
choice_d: Only Sundays are excluded; Saturdays and holidays count
explanation: When a computed period is seven days or less, intervening Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays are excluded from the computation; for longer periods, such days are included.

question: Per Rule 520-4-.02(9), what is prohibited regarding communication with Commission members about a pending contested case?
choice_a: Only the licensee is barred from communicating; opposing counsel may freely do so
choice_b: Only written communication is prohibited; phone calls are permitted
choice_c: Communication is unrestricted as long as both parties are copied
choice_d: Ex-parte communication with a Commission member or involved employee about the merits of the case, by anyone not employed by the Commission
explanation: No person not employed by the Commission shall communicate ex-parte with any Commission member or involved employee regarding the merits of a contested case; violations require immediately informing all parties.

question: Under Rule 520-4-.02(10), what is the charge rate for copies of material from an applicant/licensee's investigative file?
choice_a: $.25 per page, with a minimum charge of $5.00
choice_d: $10.00 per document regardless of page count
explanation: Charges for copies of material from the investigative file are $.25 per page with a minimum charge of $5.00, mailed by certified mail or statutory overnight delivery at the requester's expense.

question: Per Rule 520-4-.04(1), within how many days from the filing of an initial decision by the Administrative Law Judge may a party request Commission review of that decision?
explanation: Any party may request a review of an initial decision by filing the request within thirty days from the date the Administrative Law Judge filed the initial decision.

question: Under Rule 520-4-.04(5), petitions for judicial review of a Commission decision must be filed in which court?
choice_a: Any Georgia superior court chosen by the petitioner
choice_b: The Georgia Court of Appeals directly
explanation: All petitions for judicial review must be filed in accordance with the Georgia Administrative Procedure Act and must be filed in Fulton County Superior Court.

question: Per O.C.G.A. 43-40-10, what must a firm designate in order to be granted a broker's license?
choice_a: A minimum of $100,000 in operating capital
choice_b: A board of at least three licensed brokers
choice_c: A corporate resolution filed annually with the Secretary of State
choice_d: A qualifying broker, individually licensed as a broker, responsible for ensuring the firm's compliance
explanation: No broker's license shall be granted to a firm unless it designates an individual licensed as a broker as its qualifying broker, responsible for ensuring the firm and its affiliated licensees comply with the chapter and its rules.

question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-9(c)(4), if a nonresident licensee terminates affiliation with a Georgia broker, what happens to the nonresident's license unless action is taken within 30 days?
choice_a: It is automatically terminated, unless the licensee places it on inactive status or affiliates with another broker within 30 days
choice_b: It remains active indefinitely with no action required
choice_c: It converts automatically to a resident license
choice_d: It is suspended for exactly one year
explanation: If a nonresident licensee terminates affiliation with a broker, the license is automatically terminated unless the nonresident places it on inactive status or affiliates with another licensed broker within 30 days.

question: Per O.C.G.A. 43-40-19(a), within how many days must a broker notify the Commission in writing of a change in the address of the broker's place of business?
explanation: Should a broker change the address of the broker's place of business, the broker must notify the Commission in writing within 30 days of the change.

question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-23, may a county or municipal corporation levy a fixed-amount license, occupational, or professional tax on real estate brokers?
choice_b: Only counties, never municipalities, may levy such a tax
choice_c: No, except as specifically provided for in O.C.G.A. Section 48-13-17
choice_d: Only if the broker's gross revenue exceeds $500,000 annually
explanation: No county or municipal corporation may levy or collect any fixed-amount license, occupational, or professional tax on real estate brokers, except as provided in O.C.G.A. Section 48-13-17.

question: Per O.C.G.A. 43-40-24(a), what must a person allege and prove in order to maintain a court action to collect compensation for acts covered by the license law?
choice_a: That they held a valid driver's license at the time of the transaction
choice_b: That the other party was represented by an attorney
choice_d: That they were a licensed broker in Georgia at the time the cause of action arose
explanation: No person may bring or maintain a court action to collect compensation for acts covered by the chapter without alleging and proving they were a licensed broker in Georgia at the time the cause of action arose.

question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-9(b), the Commission may grant a license to a nonresident who is NOT licensed in their own state of residence, provided the applicant meets what requirement?
choice_a: The age, education, and examination requirements prescribed in O.C.G.A. Section 43-40-8
choice_b: Proof of five years' unlicensed real estate experience
choice_c: A personal recommendation from a sitting Commission member
choice_d: Nothing further; nonresidents are automatically exempt from all requirements
explanation: The Commission may grant a license to a nonresident not licensed in their state of residence if the applicant meets the age, education, and examination requirements prescribed in O.C.G.A. Section 43-40-8, the same as a resident applicant.

question: Per O.C.G.A. 43-40-19(c), a licensee transferring to a new broker may continue acting on transactions begun before the transfer for the FORMER broker only if which condition is met?
choice_a: The licensee unilaterally decides to continue without informing either broker
choice_b: Both brokers agree in writing, the enumerated transactions are specified, and the former broker agrees in writing to assume full responsibility
choice_c: The Commission issues a special dual-affiliation license
choice_d: It is never permitted under any circumstances
explanation: A transferring licensee may continue acting for the former broker on pre-transfer transactions only if both brokers agree in writing, the specific transactions are enumerated, the former broker assumes full written responsibility, and compensation terms are documented.

question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-10, what happens to a qualifying broker's license if the firm violates the chapter or its rules?
choice_a: Only the firm's license is affected; the qualifying broker's individual license is never implicated
choice_b: The violation is automatically dismissed if the firm pays a fine
choice_c: The qualifying broker's license is subject to sanction as authorized by the chapter
choice_d: Only affiliated licensees who directly committed the violation may be sanctioned
explanation: Violations of the chapter or its rules by a firm licensed as a broker subject the license of the qualifying broker to sanction as authorized by the chapter, since the qualifying broker is responsible for the firm's compliance.

question: Per O.C.G.A. 43-40-9(c), which requirement applies to a nonresident corporation or limited liability company seeking Georgia licensure?
choice_a: It must have at least ten Georgia-resident employees
choice_b: It must relocate its headquarters to Georgia
choice_c: It is exempt from any Georgia business registration requirement
choice_d: It must obtain and maintain a certificate of authority to transact business in Georgia
explanation: A nonresident corporation or limited liability company must obtain from the proper agency and maintain a certificate of authority to transact business in Georgia.

question: Under Rule 520-4-.03(1), how must service of a proposed or final decision in a contested case be made upon an applicant or licensee?
choice_a: By personal delivery or by certified mail or statutory overnight delivery to the last address of record
choice_b: By publication in a local newspaper only
choice_c: By posting on the Commission's public website only
explanation: Service of a proposed or final decision in a contested case shall be by personal delivery or by certified mail or statutory overnight delivery to the applicant/licensee's last address of record with the Commission.

question: Per Rule 520-4-.04(3), a party may move to remand a matter to the Office of State Administrative Hearings for what purpose, and under what standard is such a motion granted?
choice_a: To dismiss the case entirely, granted automatically upon request
choice_b: To take additional testimony, granted only for good cause shown
choice_c: To transfer venue to another state, granted at the Commission's sole discretion
choice_d: Remand motions are not permitted under these rules
explanation: A party may move for remand to the Office of State Administrative Hearings for purposes of taking additional testimony; such motions are granted only for good cause shown.

question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-10, can a broker's license be granted to a firm if any person acting as a licensee for that firm does not hold a real estate license?
choice_a: Yes, as long as the qualifying broker is properly licensed
choice_b: Only administrative staff are exempt from this requirement
choice_c: No -- every person acting as a licensee for the firm must hold a real estate license
choice_d: This requirement applies only to firms with more than ten employees
explanation: No broker's license shall be granted to a firm unless every person who acts as a licensee for that firm holds a real estate license.
